definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese floor mat made of woven rush grass over a rice straw core. Used as flooring in traditional Japanese rooms.

examples.japanese: この{部屋|へや}は{畳|たたみ}です。
{畳|たたみ}の{上|うえ}に{布団|ふとん}を{敷|し}きます。
examples.english: I lay out the futon on the tatami.

examples.japanese: この{部屋|へや}は{六|ろく}{畳|じょう}です。
examples.english: This room is six tatami mats in size.
examples.notes: 畳 is also used as a unit of measurement

notes:
{畳|たたみ} is both a flooring material and a unit for measuring room size.

AS A UNIT OF MEASUREMENT:
- {一|いち}{畳|じょう}: 1 tatami mat (approximately 1.65 m²)
- {六|ろく}{畳|じょう}: 6-mat room (about 10 m²)
- {八|はち}{畳|じょう}: 8-mat room (about 13 m²)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {畳|たたみ}の{部屋|へや}: tatami room
- {畳|たたみ}を{敷|し}く: to lay tatami
- {畳|たたみ}を{替|か}える: to replace tatami

CULTURAL NOTE: Shoes are never worn on tatami. The smell of fresh tatami is considered pleasant and associated with traditional Japanese aesthetics.
